# Canonical quantum Unit maps: first-source study

Twenty-two informed, complete projects were preserved before checking or
implementing the public `std::quantum::unit` and `std::quantum::finish` names.
The [recorded ordinary API decision](contract.md) specifies one ordinary Unit
argument for unit, one Q<Unit> argument for finish, zero static arguments,
Unitary action and exact coefficient +1. It is not a new constitutional
interpretation, guarantee admission or proof.

The 48 initial files are fixed by `first-files.json`, SHA-256
`55bcfcd58ea1a2c696b65b341d5513a453d26e7b82758c5f4bea7062d09e6030`.
They include every source and schema-2 edition-2026 manifest, context,
independent expected law, exact Issue section and pre-observation identity
record. No initial source was repaired. Grouped counterexamples are explicitly
labeled; a first error may mask a later condition even after implementation.

The current Git commit was `e01e98a42a00c04892617205307f2db76b5c404e`.
The existing CLI was reused without building or copying it: observed SHA-256
`25ee7a6e03d7c7b4e2c6b67754c5ad62dd40cc98aaf93a7bba09b77a5d23f280`.
These are separate observations, not an inference that a Git commit uniquely
attests an executable. All 366 selected source hashes from the preceding
actual MSRV fixed-request build record matched the current files. A separate
101-file src/stdlib/Cargo identity inventory, all initial files, the CLI and
native checker remained unchanged through these observations. The reused
native checker SHA-256 is
`39effde0f152a2c926fcea3a7f99fc2f25f9de65906be2b8c527508353c90c85`.
No fresh Rust/Lean build, audit or proof replay occurred.

There are 44 actual command observations:

| Route | Success | Rejection | Actual result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Selected `main::f` | 2 | 20 | Both existing controls pass. Nineteen new-map projects stop at `missing dependency module std::quantum`; the packaged-tree source stops at the existing sized basis limitation. |
| Finite project | 3 | 19 | Both existing controls and the packaged coherent unitor project pass. All nineteen new-map projects stop at the absent sealed public name `unit`. |

The first import failures do **not** establish the intended type, arity,
effect, owner, unused-body or zero-fold rejections. The packaged-tree result
identifies a distinct common-frontend boundary, not permission to identify
Q<(Unit,Bit)> with a tuple of separate owners. No observed rejection has been
rewritten as implementation success.

Every finite project includes an empty nullary observe main. Its check does
not execute the open f, derive its scalar coefficient or independently test a
reference state. The selected controls target f and retain their actual native
scope in JSON. All sources contain at most one physical system qubit.

`expectations.json` records the independent intended laws: both round trips
have exact +1 action with arbitrary retained references; finish does not erase
the phase in a scalar computation; controlled four eighth phases are Z;
left/right separate-owner wrappers retain owner/axis order; and the explicit
ordinary Unit argument retains complete preceding work exactly once. These
are requirements for subsequent tests and implementation, not results of this
diagnostic study. In particular, the observing-argument program's source effect
must be distinguished from a later hierarchy instrument-result profile limit.

`session.json` links the exact sources and observations; `baseline-summary.json`
summarizes only the returned diagnostics. `identity-after.json` closes the
pre-change identity comparison. `files.json` binds the completed packet's
other files. Subsequent source repairs or executions must receive new paths
and records; preserve these originals. This study closes no Issue, admits no
guarantee, and claims no general preservation, resource, realization or release
result.
